newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP proposes abolishing Japan Development Bank.
newsitem.headline: LDP proposes abolishing Japan Development Bank.

text.p: A reform panel of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) called for the abolishment of the Japan Development Bank in their proposal for reform of public financial bodies unveiled on Friday.

The LDP's proposal called for the Japan Development Bank (JDB) and the Hokkaido and Tohoku Development Corporation to be abolished, and their current operations to be transferred to a new bank to be established in 1999.
The JDB's loans and debt will be transferred to the new bank under the proposal, the LDP said in a statement.
Securitisation of the Housing Loan Corporation's loans to homeowners and the issuance of bonds should be considered, in line with progress in the reform of Japan's financial system, the LDP said.

The LDP's proposals come at a time of mounting criticism of public financial bodies such as the JDB, the Hokkaido and Tohoku Development Corp and the Housing Loan Corporation, which have been censured for being inefficient and straying into private-sector business areas that are beyond their originally stated purpose.

The fate of the JDB, which is among the largest of the 12 government-affiliated financial bodies, had been one of the focal points of the LDP's discussions about reforming and abolishing public financial bodies.
Koko Sato, chairman of the LDP panel, said the current operations of the JDB will be reviewed and scrapped where possible, before they are transferred to the new bank.
"I think it will be possible to cut roughly a third of the JDB's current operations (loans)," Sato said at a news conference held at the LDP's headquarters.

The JDB has made loans to the nation's core industries in the past, but the new bank will shift its focus to lending to regional development projects and areas more relevent to people's everyday lives, such as environmental and disaster-prevention projects, Sato said.
Sato said the LDP planned to hold discussions with its political allies and to finalise the proposal as soon as possible.
The JDB's outstanding loans totalled 15.3 trillion yen as of the end of February 1997. Its assets as of end-March 1996 were worth 15.9 trillion yen.
The Hokkaido and Tohoku Development Corp's outstanding loans totalled 1.4 trillion yen as of the end of February 1997, and its assets were worth 1.5 trillion yen as of end-March 1996.
The Housing Loan Corporation's loans totalled 69.6 trillion yen as of end-February 1997. Its assets were worth 66.6 trillion yen as of end-March 1996.
